article.title: ICE Out of NJ Demands Freedom for Junior Marte & Other Former Delaney Hall Hunger Strikers
article.content: Democracy Now! has obtained exclusive audio from inside Delaney Hall, the controversial immigrant detention center in Newark, New Jersey, operated by the for-profit prison company GEO Group. The audio was recorded over the summer during a labor and hunger strike organized by immigrant detainees. Junior Marte, an asylum seeker and father from Venezuela, was one of the organizers. He describes conditions inside the facility, including abusive treatment, medical neglect and prolonged legal limbo. “We are here unjustly, wrongfully accused of being criminals. Yet immigration officials refuse to review our cases, because they know that we are all innocent people,” Marte says in the message. The hunger and labor strike lasted for a month, with an estimated 300 detained immigrants participating in the protest. Jenny Garcia, campaign coordinator at the American Friends Service Committee of New Jersey, says that since the strikes, GEO Group and ICE have taken “every opportunity to retaliate against the strikers, the families visiting outside, and the protesters.”
